PROGRAM REPORT CURRICULUM & STANDARDS COMMITTEE Report 2025-2026-08B At the April 23, 2026 meeting of the Curriculum & Standards Committee, the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate for approval.
FOR CONFIRMATION BY THE FACULTY SENATE COLLEGE OF ARTS & SCIENCES BA – Computer Science, effective Fall 2026 Appendix A This curriculum revision represents a strategic modernization that strengthens the B.A. in Computer Science through internal reallocation of Department resources while preserving its distinctive character as a flexible, interdisciplinary degree option.
The proposed changes maintain 120 total credits while prescribing a 36-credit core.
The B.A. requires nine core CS courses compared to eleven core and three specialization courses in the B.S. program, providing a lighter computing load while ensuring foundational competency in software development, algorithms, systems, and machine learning.
BA – Film Media, effective Summer 2026 Appendix B Film media is deleting courses that have been removed from the URI catalog and adding new FLM courses to the appropriate elective pools.

BA – Journalism, effective Fall 2026 Appendix C During a curriculum retreat, members of the journalism faculty evaluated both the program learning outcomes and the curriculum for the B.A in Journalism degree program.
Based on our retreat and our focus on experiential learning in the program, we voted to adopt new requirements for our major.
These changes include eliminating the conceptual/skills designation in our current curriculum, adding additional core requirements, and altering JOR elective options so that students may pursue recommended, but not required, pathways in print, photojournalism, and multimedia/video journalism.
Several advanced courses will work directly with our new Community News Lab, which provides real-world experience to our students by having them produce news content for local media organizations.

BA – Public Relations, effective Fall 2026 Appendix D The Public Relations degree program was developed within the Communication Studies department.
In the Fall of 2024, the program moved into a new department.
The Department of Journalism and Public Relations now manages both the Journalism BA and Public Relations BA degrees.
While the PR program stands on its own, it shares many courses with Communication Studies, particularly in the three focus areas.
As the two programs have become more distinct, scheduling and course management issues have arisen.
Public Relations majors have trouble enrolling in Communication Studies courses to fulfill their focus areas.
We are proposing to amend the focus areas so s tudents have more flexibility in their elective courses.
Both the JOR/PR faculty and the Communication Studies faculty support the proposed changes (please see attached).
Please note the focus area course list remains the same with one exception, we added an additional course COM 321G.
BA – Theatre, effective Fall 2026 Appendix E The Theatre BA is currently suspended and only open to those students who are pursuing a degree in Elementary Education.

We propose reinstating the BA for all eligible students in order to serve the shifting demographic of our student body as well as refine our BFA program to introduce more rigorous standards appropriate to a pre-professional training program.
The Rhode Island Promise Act has increased the number of transfer students considerably, making it highly difficult for those students to complete a BFA in 4 years.
Additionally, the number of double majors/minors has increased making it equally difficult for those students to complete the very narrow BFA curriculum without impact to their other majors (particularly those, such as Nursing, who also have to meet clinical requirements that tend to conflict with our required courses).
A BA offers more flexibility for order of courses, thus making it more feasible for our transfer students and those completing more than one major.
URI Theatre completed an External Review in Spring of 2024.
Among their recommendations was to standardize evaluation tools across our curriculum and instate more rigorous standards for degree completion, including capstone performances and projects.

Many BFA programs also involve standards that, if not met, result in dismissal from the program.
It has never been the policy of URI theatre to dismiss students from our program except in very rare cases of academic failure.
Introducing this type of standardization is possible if we have the option to invite students to our BA program in the event that the BFA curriculum is not a good fit.
Bifurcating our program in this way allows URI Theatre to serve the widest number of students while also introducing more clear standards for our BFA students.
The reinstatement of the BA does not require any new courses or staffing.
Students in the BA program will be taking courses already offered in our existing curriculum but have more choice in terms of when and what they take.

Because our program has undergone some changes to course codes since the suspension of the BA, we include here the courses we propose for completion of the BA in Theatre: Core Courses (total of 33 credits): THE111 (Introduction to Acting), THE161 (Introduction to Stagecraft), THE181 (Script Analysis), THE221 (Introduction to Stage Management), THE250 (Costume Laboratory), THE251 (Introduction to Design), THE307 or THE338G ( Creative Dramatics or Ethics in Theatre), THE321 (Orientation to Directing), THE381 (Theatre History to 1642), THE382 (Theatre History:

Neoclassical through 19th century), and either THE351, 352, 383, 384 OR 481 (these are advanced design or special topics courses) for a total of 33 required credits.
Optional electives within the major include THE112, THE200, THE300, THE400.
For many students, this would include participating in our production season for which they receive course credit (THE200/300/400).
Students must complete a minimum of 30 credits at the 300-level or above (these may include 300-level courses offered inside the major or courses offered outside the program).

This course would benefit our clinical neuroscience students from knowledge regarding psychotropics medications that are used to treat clinical disorders (depression, anxiety, OCD, etc.) Many of the clinical neuroscience students pursue healthcare, graduate PhD programs in psychology, and medical school.

Film/Media is an interdisciplinary major offering hands-on experience in documentary, experimental, narrative, and new media production, balanced with an emphasis on international cinemas, film/media history, criticism, and theory.
Our curriculum reflects the dynamic and diverse nature of this field, approached from a perspective of film history and media theory.
Students learn to work with the evolving and overlapping technologies involved in the production of moving images (including film, digital video, 3D animation, game design, and new media), with an understanding of the broadening and globalization of their cultural and aesthetic contexts.
A wide range of courses is available to the film/media student—courses that examine the historical, theoretical, and global approaches to the analysis and creation of moving images.

The film/media program prepares students for careers in such areas as independent filmmaking; animation and media design; film and television industries; advertising, marketing, and public relations; and media criticism.
Graduates of this program are also prepared to continue with graduate studies, either in film and media production for an M.F.A., or in a master’s or doctoral program in film and media studies.
Students majoring in film/media must complete a minimum of 31 credits (maximum 46) in approved courses toward the major.

This wide range of choices in film/media courses permits students to design a major that will meet both personal and professional goals.
